## Royal regalia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monarchy_of_Thailand&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Royal regalia")]

Main articles: [Regalia of Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regalia_of_Thailand "Regalia of Thailand") and [Coronation of the Thai monarch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation_of_the_Thai_monarch "Coronation of the Thai monarch")

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Quintet_of_Royal_Regalia_of_Thailand_Photo_1926.png/330px-Quintet_of_Royal_Regalia_of_Thailand_Photo_1926.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Quintet_of_Royal_Regalia_of_Thailand_Photo_1926.png)

The [royal regalia of Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_regalia_of_Thailand "Royal regalia of Thailand") consists of five principal items.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Thailand#cite_note-32)

The present set of the [royal regalia of Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_regalia_of_Thailand "Royal regalia of Thailand") ([Thai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thai_language "Thai language"): เครื่องราชกกุธภัณฑ์, [RTGS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Thai_General_System_of_Transcription "Royal Thai General System of Transcription"):_Khrueang Raja Kakudhabhand_) together with the royal utensils, was created mostly during the reigns of King Rama I and King Rama IV, after the previous set was lost during the sack of Ayutthaya by the Burmese in 1767. The regalia are used mainly during the king's [coronation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation "Coronation") ceremony at the beginning of each reign. The regalia are presently on display in the museum of the [Grand Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Palace "Grand Palace") in Bangkok.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Thailand#cite_note-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Thailand#cite_note-60celebrations-34)

*   [Royal Nine-Tiered Umbrella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Nine-Tiered_Umbrella "Royal Nine-Tiered Umbrella") (_Phra Maha Swetachatra_; พระมหาเศวตฉัตร) – the most important regalia. Currently there are seven, distributed among various palaces.
*   [Great Crown of Victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Crown_of_Victory "Great Crown of Victory") (_Phra Maha Phichai Mongkut_; พระมหาพิชัยมงกุฎ) – the official headgear.
*   [Sword of Victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword_of_Victory "Sword of Victory") (_Phra Saeng Khan Chai Si_; พระแสงขรรค์ชัยศรี) – found at [Tonlé Sap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonl%C3%A9_Sap "Tonlé Sap") in 1784; the sword represents military power.
*   [Royal Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Staff "Royal Staff") (_Than Phra Kon_; ธารพระกร) – a symbol of justice.
*   Royal fan and [fly-whisk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fly-whisk "Fly-whisk") (_Walawijani_; วาลวีชนี) – the royal fan is made of gold, and the fly-whisk is made from the tail of a [white elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_elephant_(animal) "White elephant (animal)").
*   Royal slippers (_Chalong Phra Bat_; ฉลองพระบาท) – official footwear made of gold.

The Thai royal utensils (_Phra Khattiya Rajuprapoke_; พระขัตติยราชูปโภค) are also for the personal use of the monarch,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy_of_Thailand#cite_note-60celebrations-34) comprising:

*   the betel set
*   a water urn
*   a libation vessel
*   a receptacle

These objects are traditionally placed on either side of the king's throne or seat during royal ceremonies.

### Other symbols of kingship

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Monarchy_of_Thailand&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Other symbols of kingship")]

*   [Royal white elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_elephant "White elephant") – usually one representing each reign; the current one resides at [Dusit Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dusit_Zoo "Dusit Zoo"), and the king also has 10 others.
*   [Royal Garuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emblem_of_Thailand "Emblem of Thailand") – emblem of the king and of Thailand.
*   [Royal Standard of Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Standard_of_Thailand "Royal Standard of Thailand") – official standard of the king.
*   [Royal flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Flags_of_Thailand "Royal Flags of Thailand") – personal flags of the king and the royal family.
*   _[Sansoen Phra Barami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sansoen\_Phra\_Barami "Sansoen Phra Barami")_ – the royal anthem.
*   [Traditional Band of the Royal Family of Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakhom_band "Prakhom band") – a traditional [marching band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marching_band "Marching band") that uses Thai instruments; it accompanies the royal family and performs at ceremonies presided over by a member of the royal family.

The king is sovereign of several [Royal Orders and Decorations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_(decoration) "Order (decoration)"), the prerogative to appoint and remove any persons from these orders are at the king's discretion. However, sometimes recommendations are made by the [Cabinet of Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_Thailand "Cabinet of Thailand") and the [Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Thailand "Prime Minister of Thailand"). There are twelve Royal Orders and some of these have separate classes.

*   The Most Auspicious [Order of the Rajamitrabhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Rajamitrabhorn "Order of the Rajamitrabhorn"): Established on 11 June 1962 by King Rama IX to be bestowed upon foreign heads of state.
*   The Most Illustrious [Order of the Royal House of Chakri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Royal_House_of_Chakri "Order of the Royal House of Chakri"): Established in 1882 by King Rama V of the Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand) to commemorate the Bangkok Centennial.
*   The Ancient and Auspicious [Order of the Nine Gems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Nine_Gems "Order of the Nine Gems"): Established in 1851 by King Rama IV of the Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand). The order is bestowed upon the members of the Thai royal family and distinguished high-ranking officials who have given service to the kingdom and who are Buddhist.
*   The Most Illustrious [Order of Chula Chom Klao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Chula_Chom_Klao "Order of Chula Chom Klao"): Established on 16 November 1873 by King Rama V of The Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand) to commemorate the 90th Jubilee of the Chakri dynasty, and bears his name.
*   The [Ratana Varabhorn Order of Merit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratana_Varabhorn_Order_of_Merit "Ratana Varabhorn Order of Merit"): Established on 1 August 1911 by King Rama VI of The Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand) to reward personal service to the sovereign.
*   The Honourable [Order of Rama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Rama "Order of Rama"): Established on 22 July 1918 (B.E. 2461) by King Rama VI of the Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand), to be bestowed onto those who have rendered special military services either in peace or in wartime.
*   The Most Exalted [Order of the White Elephant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_White_Elephant "Order of the White Elephant"): Established in 1861 by King Rama IV of the Kingdom of Siam. Along with the Order of the Crown of Thailand, it is regularly awarded to government officials for each five years of service, making it Thailand's most-awarded order.
*   The Most Noble [Order of the Crown of Thailand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Crown_of_Thailand "Order of the Crown of Thailand"): Established in 1869 by King Rama V of The Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand) for Thais, the royal family, governmental employees, and foreign dignitaries for their outstanding services to the Kingdom of Thailand.
*   The Most Admirable [Order of the Direkgunabhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Direkgunabhorn "Order of the Direkgunabhorn"): Established by King Rama IX on 22 July 1991 (B.E.2534) to be bestowed upon those who have rendered devotional services to the Kingdom of Thailand.
*   The [Vallabhabhorn Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vallabhabhorn_Order "Vallabhabhorn Order"): Established on 22 March 1919 (B.E. 2461) by King Rama VI of The Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand).
*   The [Order of Ramkeerati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Ramkeerati "Order of Ramkeerati"): Established on 26 November 1987 (B.E. 2530) by King Rama IX of Thailand to be bestowed onto those who have rendered constant service and support to Boy Scout activities for at least five consecutive years.
*   The [Vajira Mala Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vajira_Mala_Order "Vajira Mala Order"): Established on 28 May 1911 (B.E. 2454) by King Rama VI of the Kingdom of Siam (now Thailand).

India first joined the [Olympic Games](https://kids.kiddle.co/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") in 1900. This made India the first country from Asia to take part! A single athlete, [Norman Pritchard](https://kids.kiddle.co/Norman_Pritchard "Norman Pritchard"), represented India. He won two silver medals in [athletics](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sport_of_athletics "Sport of athletics").

India sent its first team to the [Summer Olympic Games](https://kids.kiddle.co/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games") in 1920. Since then, India has been part of every Summer Games. India also started competing in the [Winter Olympic Games](https://kids.kiddle.co/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games") in 1964.

Indian athletes have won 41 medals so far, all at the Summer Games. For many years, the Indian Men's Field Hockey Team was super strong in the Olympics. They won eleven medals between 1928 and 1980. This included eight gold medals, with six of them won in a row from 1928 to 1956! India had its best performance ever at the 2020 Games. They won seven medals, including one gold and two silver medals.

## India's Olympic Journey

### Early Days Before Independence

[![Image 5: India hockey team 1928](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/8/81/India_hockey_team_1928.jpg/300px-India_hockey_team_1928.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:India_hockey_team_1928.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:India_hockey_team_1928.jpg "Enlarge")

 Indian field hockey team that won the gold medal at the 1928 Olympics

India's first time at the Olympics was in 1900. Back then, India was part of [British India](https://kids.kiddle.co/British_Raj "British Raj"). As mentioned, it was the first Asian country to join the Games. [Norman Pritchard](https://kids.kiddle.co/Norman_Pritchard "Norman Pritchard") was the only athlete from India. He won two silver medals in athletics. India ranked 19th in medals that year, which is still its best rank ever!

India did not compete in the next three Summer Olympics. Then, in 1920, a businessman named Dorabji Tata helped India get a spot on the [International Olympic Committee](https://kids.kiddle.co/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee"). This allowed India to compete on its own at the 1920 Summer Olympics. India sent six athletes, including four runners and two [wrestlers](https://kids.kiddle.co/Wrestling_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Wrestling at the Summer Olympics").

The Indian Olympic movement grew in the 1920s. In 1927, the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) was officially recognized. This group helps develop sports in India and picks teams for the Olympics. For the [1928 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1928_Summer_Olympics "1928 Summer Olympics") in [Amsterdam](https://kids.kiddle.co/Amsterdam "Amsterdam"), India sent eight athletes. The Indian Hockey Federation also sent the men's hockey team. This team won India's first ever Olympic gold medal in Amsterdam! It was also the first gold medal won by any Asian country in the modern Olympics.

[![Image 6: Indian-Hockey-Team-Berlin-1936](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/8/8e/Indian-Hockey-Team-Berlin-1936.jpg/300px-Indian-Hockey-Team-Berlin-1936.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Indian-Hockey-Team-Berlin-1936.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Indian-Hockey-Team-Berlin-1936.jpg "Enlarge")

 Indian hockey team at the 1936 Berlin Olympics

The Indian hockey team continued its winning streak. They won three gold medals in a row from 1928 to 1936. In 1932, they beat the United States 24–1, which is the biggest win in Olympic history! In the 1936 final, they beat Germany 8–1.

### After India Became Independent

[![Image 7: Hockey Nederland India. Elftal India, Bestanddeelnr 902-9315](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/52/Hockey_Nederland_India._Elftal_India%2C_Bestanddeelnr_902-9315.jpg/300px-Hockey_Nederland_India._Elftal_India%2C_Bestanddeelnr_902-9315.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Hockey_Nederland_India._Elftal_India,_Bestanddeelnr_902-9315.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Hockey_Nederland_India._Elftal_India,_Bestanddeelnr_902-9315.jpg "Enlarge")

 Indian field hockey team that won the first gold medal after independence at the 1948 London Olympics

India became an independent country in 1947. It sent its first team as an independent nation to the [1948 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1948_Summer_Olympics "1948 Summer Olympics") in [London](https://kids.kiddle.co/London "London"). India sent 79 athletes who competed in ten sports. This included India's first time in arts, [boxing](https://kids.kiddle.co/Boxing_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Boxing at the Summer Olympics"), [cycling](https://kids.kiddle.co/Cycling_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Cycling at the Summer Olympics"), [football](https://kids.kiddle.co/Football_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Football at the Summer Olympics"), and [water polo](https://kids.kiddle.co/Water_polo_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Water polo at the Summer Olympics"). The Indian field hockey team won the only medal, a gold. This was India's first medal as an independent country.

The [1952 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1952_Summer_Olympics "1952 Summer Olympics") were special because India sent women competitors for the first time. The team had 64 athletes, including four women. Wrestler K. D. Jadhav won a bronze medal. This was the first individual medal for independent India. The Indian field hockey team won its sixth straight gold medal in 1956. In the [1960 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1960_Summer_Olympics "1960 Summer Olympics") in [Rome](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rome "Rome"), the hockey team won a silver medal after losing to Pakistan. This was their first loss in the Olympics since 1928.

India first competed in the [Winter Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games") in [1964](https://kids.kiddle.co/1964_Winter_Olympics "1964 Winter Olympics") in [Innsbruck](https://kids.kiddle.co/Innsbruck "Innsbruck"). Jeremy Bujakowski competed in [alpine skiing](https://kids.kiddle.co/Alpine_skiing_at_the_Winter_Olympics "Alpine skiing at the Winter Olympics"). Later that year, at the [1964 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1964_Summer_Olympics "1964 Summer Olympics") in [Tokyo](https://kids.kiddle.co/Tokyo "Tokyo"), the men's field hockey team won another gold medal. This was India's only medal at those Games.

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Paes_US16_(11)_(29569576630).jpg "Enlarge")

[Leander Paes](https://kids.kiddle.co/Leander_Paes "Leander Paes") won a bronze medal in 1996. This was India's first Olympic medal in almost 16 years.

India sent its smallest team since independence to the [1968 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1968_Summer_Olympics "1968 Summer Olympics") in [Mexico City](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mexico_City "Mexico City"). India did not compete in the Winter Olympics from 1972 to 1984. In the [1972 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1972_Summer_Olympics "1972 Summer Olympics") in [Munich](https://kids.kiddle.co/Munich "Munich"), the men's field hockey team won a bronze medal. In [1976 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1976_Summer_Olympics "1976 Summer Olympics") in [Montreal](https://kids.kiddle.co/Montreal "Montreal"), India did not win any medals. This was the first time since 1924.

At the [1980 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1980_Summer_Olympics "1980 Summer Olympics") in [Moscow](https://kids.kiddle.co/Moscow "Moscow"), the men's hockey team won their eighth Olympic gold medal. This was their last gold medal in hockey at the Olympics. India did not win any medals in the next three Summer Olympics (1984, 1988, 1992). India returned to the Winter Olympics in [1988](https://kids.kiddle.co/1988_Winter_Olympics "1988 Winter Olympics"). The team included the first Indian woman participant, Shailaja Kumar. In 1996, tennis player [Leander Paes](https://kids.kiddle.co/Leander_Paes "Leander Paes") won a bronze medal. This was India's first Olympic medal in almost 16 years! He was also the first Indian individual medalist since 1952.

### India in the 21st Century

[![Image 9: Olympic Freestyle Wrestling (66 kg - Medalists)](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/8/86/Olympic_Freestyle_Wrestling_%2866_kg_-_Medalists%29.jpg/300px-Olympic_Freestyle_Wrestling_%2866_kg_-_Medalists%29.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Olympic_Freestyle_Wrestling_(66_kg_-_Medalists).jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Olympic_Freestyle_Wrestling_(66_kg_-_Medalists).jpg "Enlarge")

[Sushil Kumar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sushil_Kumar "Sushil Kumar") (left) was the first Indian athlete to win more than one individual Olympic medal after independence.

At the [2000 Sydney Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics"), [Karnam Malleswari](https://kids.kiddle.co/Karnam_Malleswari "Karnam Malleswari") won a bronze medal in weightlifting. This was the first-ever Olympic medal won by an Indian woman! In 2004, shooter [Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore](https://kids.kiddle.co/Rajyavardhan_Singh_Rathore "Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore") won a silver medal.

The [2008 Beijing Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") was a great success for India. The country won three medals, including one gold and two bronze. [Abhinav Bindra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Abhinav_Bindra "Abhinav Bindra") became the first Indian to win an individual gold medal! He won in men's air rifle. [Vijender Singh](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vijender_Singh "Vijender Singh") won India's first Olympic medal in boxing. [Sushil Kumar](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sushil_Kumar "Sushil Kumar") won a bronze in wrestling.

The [2012 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics") saw India win its highest number of medals at the time: six medals (two silver and four bronze). Sushil Kumar won a silver medal, becoming the first Indian since independence to win multiple individual Olympic medals. Shooter Vijay Kumar won another silver. [Saina Nehwal](https://kids.kiddle.co/Saina_Nehwal "Saina Nehwal") won India's first medal in badminton. Boxer [Mary Kom](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mary_Kom "Mary Kom") became the first Indian woman to win a medal in boxing.

[![Image 10: Mary Kom with young sportsperson](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/a/a4/Mary_Kom_with_young_sportsperson.jpg/300px-Mary_Kom_with_young_sportsperson.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Mary_Kom_with_young_sportsperson.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Mary_Kom_with_young_sportsperson.jpg "Enlarge")

[Mary Kom](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mary_Kom "Mary Kom") won India's first medal in women's boxing at the [2012 Games](https://kids.kiddle.co/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics").

In 2014, the Indian Olympic Association was temporarily suspended. This meant some Indian athletes competed as independent participants at the [2014 Winter Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2014_Winter_Olympics "2014 Winter Olympics"). But the suspension was lifted during the Games, and two athletes then competed under the Indian flag.

For the [2016 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2016_Summer_Olympics "2016 Summer Olympics"), India sent over 100 athletes for the first time. India won two medals: one silver and one bronze. Shuttler [P. V. Sindhu](https://kids.kiddle.co/P._V._Sindhu "P. V. Sindhu") won a silver medal, becoming the first Indian woman to win an Olympic silver. Sakshi Malik became the first Indian female wrestler to win an Olympic medal, earning a bronze.

[![Image 11: Neeraj Chopra Olympic gold medalist](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/f/fb/Neeraj_Chopra_Olympic_gold_medalist.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Neeraj_Chopra_Olympic_gold_medalist.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Neeraj_Chopra_Olympic_gold_medalist.jpg "Enlarge")

[Neeraj Chopra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Neeraj_Chopra "Neeraj Chopra") won India's first ever athletics gold medal in [2020](https://kids.kiddle.co/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics"). He then won a silver in [2024](https://kids.kiddle.co/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics").

India sent its largest team ever to the [2020 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2020_Summer_Olympics "2020 Summer Olympics"), with 119 athletes. This was India's most successful Games, with seven medals! These included one gold, two silver, and four bronze. [Neeraj Chopra](https://kids.kiddle.co/Neeraj_Chopra "Neeraj Chopra") won India's first ever gold medal in athletics (javelin throw). Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won India's first silver medal in [weightlifting](https://kids.kiddle.co/Weightlifting_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Weightlifting at the Summer Olympics"). P. V. Sindhu became the first Indian woman to win medals in two different Summer Games. The men's field hockey team won a bronze medal, their first Olympic medal since 1980!

At the [2024 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics"), India won six medals: one silver and five bronze. Three of these were in [shooting](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shooting_at_the_2024_Summer_Olympics "Shooting at the 2024 Summer Olympics"). Neeraj Chopra won a silver medal in javelin throw, making him the first Indian to win both a gold and a silver at the Olympics. Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals in shooting. She became the first Indian since independence to win two medals in a single Olympics. The men's field hockey team won a bronze medal for the second Olympics in a row. Aman Sehrawat won a bronze in wrestling, becoming the youngest Indian to win an Olympic medal.

## India's Men's Field Hockey Team at the Olympics

Main article: [Field hockey at the Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/Field_hockey_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Field hockey at the Summer Olympics")

The Indian Men's Field Hockey Team has won the most medals in field hockey at the Olympics. They have won 13 medals, including eight gold medals. Six of these gold medals were won in a row from 1928 to 1956!

**Xi Jinping** (born 15 June 1953) is a Chinese politician. He has been the top leader of China since 2012. This means he is the [General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party](https://kids.kiddle.co/General_Secretary_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party") (CCP) and the chairman of China's military. Since 2013, Xi has also been the [President of China](https://kids.kiddle.co/President_of_China "President of China"). He is the first CCP leader born after the People's Republic of China was founded in 1949.

Xi's father was a Chinese communist leader. During the [Cultural Revolution](https://kids.kiddle.co/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution"), his father faced difficulties, and Xi was sent to live in a rural area. He lived in a cave house in Liangjiahe village. There, he joined the CCP and worked as a local leader. After studying [chemical engineering](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chemical_engineering "Chemical engineering") at [Tsinghua University](https://kids.kiddle.co/Tsinghua_University "Tsinghua University"), Xi began to rise in politics. He worked in coastal provinces like [Fujian](https://kids.kiddle.co/Fujian "Fujian") and [Zhejiang](https://kids.kiddle.co/Zhejiang "Zhejiang"). In 2007, he became a member of the CCP's top leadership group, the [Politburo Standing Committee](https://kids.kiddle.co/Politburo_Standing_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "Politburo Standing Committee of the Chinese Communist Party"). In 2008, he became the [Vice President of China](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vice_President_of_China "Vice President of China"). He was seen as the next leader of China.

As China's leader, Xi has focused on making the country stronger. He started a big campaign against corruption. This campaign led to many officials being removed from their positions. He also introduced policies to help people become more prosperous and reduce poverty. He has supported state-owned businesses and focused on developing new technologies. During the COVID-19 pandemic, he led China's "zero-COVID" policy. This policy aimed to stop the virus from spreading.

In foreign policy, Xi has made China more assertive on the world stage. He has worked to expand China's influence globally, especially through projects like the [Belt and Road Initiative](https://kids.kiddle.co/Belt_and_Road_Initiative "Belt and Road Initiative"). He has also focused on China's relationships with countries like the United States and those in Asia. Under his leadership, China has increased its military strength.

Since Xi became leader, there have been changes in China's society. Censorship and mass surveillance have increased. There have also been concerns about human rights, especially regarding ethnic minorities. In 2018, China's constitution was changed to remove term limits for the president. This allowed Xi to serve more than two terms. His political ideas, known as Xi Jinping Thought, are now part of China's official documents. In October 2022, Xi began his third term as the CCP General Secretary. He was re-elected as president in March 2023.

## Early Life and Education

Xi Jinping was born in [Beijing](https://kids.kiddle.co/Beijing "Beijing") on 15 June 1953. He was the third child of [Xi Zhongxun](https://kids.kiddle.co/Xi_Zhongxun "Xi Zhongxun"), a well-known communist leader. His father held important jobs after the People's Republic of China was founded in 1949. Xi had two older sisters.

Xi attended schools in Beijing in the 1960s. In 1963, when he was ten, his father faced political difficulties. His father was sent to work in a factory. In 1966, the [Cultural Revolution](https://kids.kiddle.co/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution") began. This period stopped many students from going to school. Xi's family home was searched, and one of his sisters died due to the events of that time.

His mother was forced to speak against his father in public. His father was later put in prison in 1968. In 1968, Xi decided to leave Beijing for the countryside. On 13 January 1969, he arrived in Liangjiahe Village in [Shaanxi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shaanxi "Shaanxi") province. This was part of a movement where young people were sent to rural areas. Life in Liangjiahe was very different from Beijing. Xi had to get used to many challenges, like dealing with fleas, finding enough food, and doing hard labor. This experience helped him understand the lives of poor farmers.

After a few months, he tried to return to Beijing but was arrested. He was sent to a work camp. He later went back to Liangjiahe. He became the local party secretary there. He lived in a yaodong, which is a type of cave house.

Xi spent seven years in the countryside. In 1973, he was assigned to another village to help with social education. He worked well with the villagers. He applied to join the Chinese Communist Party many times. His father's political problems made it difficult. But in early 1974, his application was finally approved. He then became the Party branch chairman of Liangjiahe.

After becoming a leader, Xi learned about [biogas](https://kids.kiddle.co/Biogas "Biogas") technology from another region. He brought this idea back to Liangjiahe. This helped solve fuel shortages in his village. He also led projects to dig wells for water, start small industries, and plant tobacco. In 1975, he was recommended for [Tsinghua University](https://kids.kiddle.co/Tsinghua_University "Tsinghua University"). From 1975 to 1979, he studied [chemical engineering](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chemical_engineering "Chemical engineering") there.

## Early Political Career

### Starting in Government

After graduating in 1979, Xi worked in government offices. He served as a secretary to Geng Biao, who was then the Minister of Defense.

### Working in Hebei

In 1982, Xi became a deputy party secretary in [Zhengding County](https://kids.kiddle.co/Zhengding_County "Zhengding County"), Hebei province. He worked with another leader to write a letter to the central government. They wanted to reduce the amount of crops farmers had to give to the government. Their efforts helped farmers earn more money.

As the party secretary of Zhengding County in 1983, Xi started many projects. He worked on developing local talents and building parks. He also helped restore a famous temple. He brought in a TV production company to film a show in Zhengding. This helped boost tourism and brought in a lot of money for the county. In 1985, Xi visited [Iowa](https://kids.kiddle.co/Iowa "Iowa"), USA, to learn about farming. After this trip, he was moved to Xiamen in Fujian province.

### Leadership in Fujian

Xi arrived in Xiamen in 1985. He helped create the city's first long-term development plan. He also worked on projects like preparing for Xiamen Airlines and improving roads. He married [Peng Liyuan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Peng_Liyuan "Peng Liyuan") while in Xiamen.

In 1988, he became the party secretary of Ningde. This area was not as developed as other parts of Fujian. Xi worked on reducing poverty and strengthening the local CCP. He wrote a book about his experiences there called _Getting out of Poverty_. In 1990, he became the Municipal Committee Secretary of [Fuzhou City](https://kids.kiddle.co/Fuzhou "Fuzhou").

In 1997, he became an alternate member of the 15th CCP Central Committee. He was promoted to Vice Governor of Fujian in 1999 and then governor in 2000. He focused on attracting investment and developing industries. He also worked on improving city areas and helping people on Pingtan Island escape poverty. He oversaw the development of "Digital Fujian," which improved government services.

### Leading in Zhejiang

In 2002, Xi moved to [Zhejiang](https://kids.kiddle.co/Zhejiang "Zhejiang") province. He became the provincial Party Committee secretary. This was his first time holding a top provincial job. In 2002, he became a full member of the 16th Central Committee. This marked his move to the national political stage. While in Zhejiang, the economy grew quickly. Xi was known for being tough on corrupt officials. This gained him attention from China's top leaders.

### Time in Shanghai

In 2007, Xi was transferred to [Shanghai](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shanghai "Shanghai") to become the party secretary. He served there for seven months. In Shanghai, Xi focused on keeping the local party united. He avoided controversy and followed party rules strictly. He reportedly refused to take a special train for himself, saying it was only for "national leaders."

## Becoming a Top Leader

[![Image 5: President George W. Bush with Vice President Xi Jinping](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/b/ba/President_George_W._Bush_with_Vice_President_Xi_Jinping.jpg/300px-President_George_W._Bush_with_Vice_President_Xi_Jinping.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:President_George_W._Bush_with_Vice_President_Xi_Jinping.jpg)

 Xi Jinping greeting U.S. president [George W. Bush](https://kids.kiddle.co/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush") in August 2008

[![Image 6: Dmitry Medvedev in China 28 September 2010-6](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/5/52/Dmitry_Medvedev_in_China_28_September_2010-6.jpeg/300px-Dmitry_Medvedev_in_China_28_September_2010-6.jpeg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Dmitry_Medvedev_in_China_28_September_2010-6.jpeg)

 Xi Jinping with Russian president [Dmitry Medvedev](https://kids.kiddle.co/Dmitry_Medvedev "Dmitry Medvedev") on 28 September 2010

In October 2007, Xi was appointed to the nine-member [Politburo Standing Committee](https://kids.kiddle.co/Politburo_Standing_Committee_of_the_Chinese_Communist_Party "Politburo Standing Committee of the Chinese Communist Party") (PSC). This showed he was likely to become China's next leader. In March 2008, he was elected [Vice President of China](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vice_President_of_China "Vice President of China"). After this, Xi took on many important tasks. He helped prepare for the [2008 Summer Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2008_Summer_Olympics "2008 Summer Olympics") in Beijing. He also became the main government figure for Hong Kong and Macau affairs. He visited disaster areas after the [2008 Sichuan earthquake](https://kids.kiddle.co/2008_Sichuan_earthquake "2008 Sichuan earthquake"). His first foreign trip as vice president was to North Korea and other countries in June 2008.

Xi's path to becoming the top leader seemed clear. However, another politician, Bo Xilai, was rising quickly. Many thought Bo might challenge Xi. But Bo's political career ended due to a scandal. This cleared the way for Xi to become the leader without major challengers.

People who knew Xi described him as thoughtful and stable. Former Singaporean Prime Minister [Lee Kuan Yew](https://kids.kiddle.co/Lee_Kuan_Yew "Lee Kuan Yew") compared him to [Nelson Mandela](https://kids.kiddle.co/Nelson_Mandela "Nelson Mandela"). He said Xi was a person with "enormous emotional stability." Former U.S. Treasury Secretary [Henry Paulson](https://kids.kiddle.co/Henry_Paulson "Henry Paulson") said Xi "knows how to get things over the goal line."

### Trips as Vice President

In February 2009, Xi traveled to Latin America. He visited Mexico, Jamaica, Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil, and Malta. In Mexico, he spoke about China's role during the global financial crisis. He said China's ability to feed its large population was a great contribution to humanity. He also said that China does not "export revolution" or "hunger and poverty."

[![Image 7: Xi Jinping Iowa house](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/4d/Xi_Jinping_Iowa_house.jpg/300px-Xi_Jinping_Iowa_house.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Xi_Jinping_Iowa_house.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Xi_Jinping_Iowa_house.jpg "Enlarge")

 The Muscatine, Iowa house where Xi stayed with an American family during a 1985 agricultural visit to the United States. The home was turned into a museum decades later.

In October 2009, he visited several European countries. In December 2009, he visited Japan, South Korea, Cambodia, and Myanmar. In February 2012, he visited the United States, Ireland, and Turkey. In the U.S., he met with President [Barack Obama](https://kids.kiddle.co/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") and Vice President [Joe Biden](https://kids.kiddle.co/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden"). He also visited [Iowa](https://kids.kiddle.co/Iowa "Iowa"), where he met the family who hosted him during his 1985 trip.

### Becoming China's Top Leader

On 15 November 2012, Xi was elected as the General Secretary of the CCP. He also became the chairman of the military commission. This made him the formal leader of the CCP and the informal top leader of China. He was the first top leader born after the founding of the People's Republic of China. The next day, he introduced the new members of the Politburo Standing Committee.

In his first speech as General Secretary, Xi spoke simply. He talked about what ordinary people hoped for. He mentioned "better education, more stable jobs, better income, more reliable social security, medical care of a higher standard, more comfortable living conditions, and a more beautiful environment." He also promised to fight corruption.

In December 2012, Xi visited [Guangdong](https://kids.kiddle.co/Guangdong "Guangdong"). This was his first trip outside Beijing as General Secretary. He called for more economic reforms and a stronger military. His trip was seen as following in the footsteps of [Deng Xiaoping](https://kids.kiddle.co/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping"), who also made an important trip to the south. Xi often spoke about the "Chinese Dream" during this trip. He said it was a dream of a strong nation and a strong military.

Xi was elected President of China on 14 March 2013. He received almost all votes from the 12th National People's Congress. He replaced [Hu Jintao](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hu_Jintao "Hu Jintao"), who retired. Soon after his election, Xi discussed cybersecurity and North Korea with U.S. President Barack Obama.

## Xi Jinping's Leadership

### Strengthening Power

[![Image 8: 抗战胜利70周年阅兵演练](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/9/98/%E6%8A%97%E6%88%98%E8%83%9C%E5%88%A970%E5%91%A8%E5%B9%B4%E9%98%85%E5%85%B5%E6%BC%94%E7%BB%83.jpg/300px-%E6%8A%97%E6%88%98%E8%83%9C%E5%88%A970%E5%91%A8%E5%B9%B4%E9%98%85%E5%85%B5%E6%BC%94%E7%BB%83.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:%E6%8A%97%E6%88%98%E8%83%9C%E5%88%A970%E5%91%A8%E5%B9%B4%E9%98%85%E5%85%B5%E6%BC%94%E7%BB%83.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:%E6%8A%97%E6%88%98%E8%83%9C%E5%88%A970%E5%91%A8%E5%B9%B4%E9%98%85%E5%85%B5%E6%BC%94%E7%BB%83.jpg "Enlarge")

 Portrait of Xi in Beijing, September 2015

Many experts say Xi is the most powerful Chinese leader since [Mao Zedong](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong"). He has brought more power to himself. He created special working groups that he leads. This helps him make decisions more directly.

In 2018, China's constitution was changed. This removed the term limits for the president and vice president. This meant Xi could serve more than two terms as president. He was reappointed as president, and [Li Keqiang](https://kids.kiddle.co/Li_Keqiang "Li Keqiang") was reappointed premier. Xi explained that this change was to match his other powerful roles, which do not have term limits.

In November 2021, the CCP passed a "historical resolution." This document looked back at the party's history. It was only the third such document in the party's history. This resolution further strengthened Xi's position. In October 2022, Xi was re-elected as General Secretary for a third term. This made him the first party leader since Mao Zedong to serve a third term. The new Politburo Standing Committee, chosen after the Congress, included many people close to Xi. In March 2023, Xi was again re-elected as president.

### Focus on Anti-Corruption

Xi promised to fight corruption as soon as he became leader. He said corruption was a big challenge for the party. He introduced rules to stop corruption and waste among officials. He vowed to go after both high-ranking officials ("tigers") and lower-level officials ("flies").

His campaign led to many important officials being investigated and removed. This included former military leaders and top security officials. Special teams were sent out to check on party organizations across the country. These teams helped find and investigate corrupt officials. Within the first two years, over 200,000 officials received warnings or punishments.

Some critics say the anti-corruption campaign was also used to remove political opponents. Xi created a new anti-corruption agency, the National Supervision Commission. This agency is very powerful. By 2023, about 2.3 million government officials had been investigated.

### Controlling Information

Since Xi became General Secretary, censorship has increased. He stated that state media must support the party's views. His government has put more restrictions on the internet. He believes in "internet sovereignty," meaning each country should control its own internet. For example, all versions of Wikipedia were blocked in China in April 2019.

A law passed in 2013 allowed prison terms for bloggers who shared "defamatory" content too many times. Many bloggers stopped writing about sensitive topics.

### Economy and Technology

Xi was first seen as someone who would bring more market reforms. His government said that market forces would play a "decisive" role in the economy. This meant reducing government involvement in some areas. He launched the Shanghai Free-Trade Zone in 2013. However, some experts said reforms slowed down by 2017.

China's economy has grown significantly under Xi. Its size doubled from 2012 to 2023. Xi has emphasized "high-quality growth" over just fast growth. He said other issues like environmental protection are important. He made ending extreme poverty a key goal. By 2021, he declared a "complete victory" over extreme poverty.

Xi has also focused on developing advanced manufacturing and technology. He promoted the "Made in China 2025" plan. This plan aims to make China self-reliant in key technologies. Spending on research and development has greatly increased. China has made big advances in areas like electric vehicles and solar panels.

Since 2021, Xi has promoted "common prosperity." This means wealth for everyone, not just a few. This idea has led to new rules for large tech companies and tutoring industries. China also introduced strict rules for private tutoring companies.

### Government Reforms

In November 2013, the Communist Party announced big reforms. These included changes to economic and social policies. Xi also created a new National Security Commission. This helped him take more control over national security.

Another group, the Central Leading Group for Comprehensively Deepening Reforms, was formed. This group, also led by Xi, oversees the reforms. These reforms were seen as very important. The party also decided to end the "re-education through labor" system. This system had faced much criticism. In 2016, China replaced the [one-child policy](https://kids.kiddle.co/One-child_policy "One-child policy") with a two-child policy. In 2021, all family size limits were removed.

#### Military Changes

Since 2012, Xi has worked to modernize China's military, the [People's Liberation Army](https://kids.kiddle.co/People%27s_Liberation_Army "People's Liberation Army"). He has taken a direct role in military reform. He has emphasized that the party must have "absolute control over the army."

In 2015, Xi announced a reduction of 300,000 troops. This brought the army's size to 2 million. In 2016, he changed the military's command structure. He reduced the number of large military regions and created new agencies that report directly to the military commission. He also created two new branches of the army.

In 2016, Xi was named commander-in-chief of the country's new Joint Operations Command Center. This showed his strong leadership. China's military budget has more than doubled under Xi. The PLA Navy has grown quickly. China has also expanded its nuclear weapons.

### Foreign Relations

Xi has taken a stronger stance on foreign affairs. He wants China to be a major global power. He believes China should be confident in its own values. Xi has promoted "major-country diplomacy." This means China acts more boldly on the world stage. His foreign policy ideas are called "Xi Jinping Thought on Diplomacy."

He has said that "the East is rising and the West is declining." He believes the Western world is facing challenges. Xi has also talked about building a "community with a shared future for mankind." This suggests China wants a new global order.

[![Image 11: Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping having tea at the garden of Zhongnanhai (2024-05-16) 2](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/4/45/Vladimir_Putin_and_Xi_Jinping_having_tea_at_the_garden_of_Zhongnanhai_%282024-05-16%29_2.jpg/300px-Vladimir_Putin_and_Xi_Jinping_having_tea_at_the_garden_of_Zhongnanhai_%282024-05-16%29_2.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Vladimir_Putin_and_Xi_Jinping_having_tea_at_the_garden_of_Zhongnanhai_(2024-05-16)_2.jpg)

Xi has focused on increasing China's "international discourse power." This means telling China's story better to the world. He has also launched global initiatives for development, security, and civilization.

#### Relations with Other Countries

*   **Africa:** China has good relationships with most African countries. Xi has promised to help some African countries with their debts.
*   **Asia:** Relations with North Korea have improved since 2018. China and South Korea signed a free-trade agreement in 2015. Relations with Japan have had ups and downs due to island disputes. China has built and militarized islands in the South China Sea. Relations with India have faced challenges, including border disputes. Xi has also worked to strengthen ties with countries in the Middle East.
*   **Europe:** China wants the European Union to remain neutral in its relations with the U.S. Xi has built stronger ties with Russia, especially since 2014. During the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Xi expressed support for Russia on some issues.
*   **United States:** Xi has called for a "new type of great-power relations" with the U.S. Relations became more difficult after 2017, leading to a trade war.

### National Security Focus

Xi has put a lot of effort into national security. He calls for a "holistic national security architecture." This means security in all parts of the country and party. He introduced this idea in 2014. It includes political, economic, military, and cultural security.

His government has passed many laws related to national security. These include laws on counterespionage, counterterrorism, and cybersecurity. China's mass surveillance network has grown significantly under Xi.

### Hong Kong Policies

[![Image 12: 2019-10-01 Demonstration Hong Kong 11](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/1/14/2019-10-01_Demonstration_Hong_Kong_11.jpg/300px-2019-10-01_Demonstration_Hong_Kong_11.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:2019-10-01_Demonstration_Hong_Kong_11.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:2019-10-01_Demonstration_Hong_Kong_11.jpg "Enlarge")

[Hong Kong protesters](https://kids.kiddle.co/2019%E2%80%9320_Hong_Kong_protests "2019–20 Hong Kong protests") throw eggs at Xi Jinping's portrait on [National Day](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_Day_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China "National Day of the People's Republic of China").

Under Xi's leadership, China has worked to integrate [Hong Kong](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hong_Kong "Hong Kong") more closely with mainland China. This includes projects like the [Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge](https://kids.kiddle.co/Hong_Kong%E2%80%93Zhuhai%E2%80%93Macau_Bridge "Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge"). These efforts have led to concerns about reduced freedoms in Hong Kong.

In 2014, China's government stated it had "comprehensive jurisdiction" over Hong Kong. In 2020, a national security law was passed in Hong Kong. This law greatly increased government control over political opposition. It was seen as a way to bring Hong Kong closer to the mainland. Xi visited Hong Kong in 2017 and 2022 for important anniversaries.

### Taiwan Relations

[![Image 13: 2015 Ma–Xi Meeting 08](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/f/f2/2015_Ma%E2%80%93Xi_Meeting_08.jpg/300px-2015_Ma%E2%80%93Xi_Meeting_08.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:2015_Ma%E2%80%93Xi_Meeting_08.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:2015_Ma%E2%80%93Xi_Meeting_08.jpg "Enlarge")

 Xi Jinping met with then-Taiwanese president [Ma Ying-jeou](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ma_Ying-jeou "Ma Ying-jeou") in November 2015 in their capacity as the leader of mainland China and Taiwan respectively.

In November 2015, Xi met with then-Taiwanese president [Ma Ying-jeou](https://kids.kiddle.co/Ma_Ying-jeou "Ma Ying-jeou"). This was the first meeting between leaders from both sides since 1950. Xi said that China and Taiwan are "one family." However, relations became more difficult after [Tsai Ing-wen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Tsai_Ing-wen "Tsai Ing-wen") became Taiwan's president in 2016.

In 2017, Xi used stronger language about potential Taiwan independence. He said China would "never allow any person, any organisation, or any political party to split any part of the Chinese territory from China." In January 2019, he said China would not promise to avoid using force to achieve unification.

### Human Rights Concerns

Since Xi became leader, there have been concerns about human rights in China. Some groups say that the situation has worsened. There have been crackdowns on activists and lawyers.

In some areas, there have been reports of policies affecting religious groups. For example, in Jiangxi province, some Christians were told to replace pictures of Jesus with pictures of Xi Jinping.

Policies towards ethnic minorities have also changed. The government has focused on assimilation. In [Xinjiang](https://kids.kiddle.co/Xinjiang "Xinjiang"), following several attacks, Xi launched a campaign in 2014. This campaign involved mass detentions and surveillance of ethnic [Uyghurs](https://kids.kiddle.co/Uyghur_people "Uyghur people"). Many people were held in internment camps. Human rights groups have described these camps as places where Uyghurs and other minorities are forced to adopt Han Chinese culture. Some international reports have raised concerns about these actions.

Xi has visited Xinjiang multiple times. He has urged local officials to listen to people and preserve ethnic minority culture. He also said the region should open up more for tourism.

### COVID-19 Pandemic Response

On 20 January 2020, Xi first spoke about the emerging [COVID-19 pandemic](https://kids.kiddle.co/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") in Wuhan. He ordered efforts to stop the virus from spreading. The government responded with lockdowns and censorship. He met with the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) on 28 January.

[![Image 14: Sergio Mattarella and Xi Jinping 2019](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/2/29/Sergio_Mattarella_and_Xi_Jinping_2019.jpg/225px-Sergio_Mattarella_and_Xi_Jinping_2019.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Sergio_Mattarella_and_Xi_Jinping_2019.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Sergio_Mattarella_and_Xi_Jinping_2019.jpg "Enlarge")

 Italian president [Sergio Mattarella](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sergio_Mattarella "Sergio Mattarella") with Xi in March 2019

After controlling the outbreak in Wuhan, Xi supported a "dynamic zero-COVID policy." This policy aimed to control the virus as much as possible within China. It involved local lockdowns and mass testing. This approach was initially praised but later criticized for its impact on the economy and people's lives. A strict lockdown in Shanghai in 2022 caused difficulties for millions.

At the 20th CCP Congress in October 2022, Xi confirmed the continuation of the zero-COVID policy. However, protests against the policy broke out in November 2022. These protests occurred in many major cities. The government then eased COVID-19 restrictions in December 2022.

### Environmental Policies

Xi sees environmental protection as a top priority for China. He uses the metaphor of "two mountains." This means that while mountains of gold and silver are valuable, "green mountains with clear waters are more valuable." This slogan means that economic growth must also protect the environment.

In September 2020, Xi announced that China would aim to reach carbon neutrality before 2060. This goal would significantly help reduce global temperature rise. He also said China would not build new coal power projects abroad.

### Leadership Style

Xi is known for being a very private leader. Not much is publicly known about how he makes political decisions. His speeches are often released months after he gives them. He rarely holds press conferences. Reports suggest Xi prefers to be very involved in the details of governance. He reportedly reviews every major policy document himself.

Xi emphasizes certain rules for Communist Party members. He calls for them to be humble and hardworking. He also encourages "self-criticism." This is meant to make officials seem less corrupt and more popular.

## Political Ideas

### The Chinese Dream

[![Image 15: Lujiazui 2016](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/e/e6/Lujiazui_2016.jpg/300px-Lujiazui_2016.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Lujiazui_2016.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Lujiazui_2016.jpg "Enlarge")

 According to _Qiushi_, the Chinese Dream is about Chinese prosperity, collective effort, socialism, and national glory.

Xi and CCP thinkers created the phrase "Chinese Dream." This describes his big plans for China. Xi first used this phrase in November 2012. It has since become his main political slogan. The "Chinese Dream" is linked to the idea of the "great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation." It is about China becoming strong and prosperous.

### Culture and Values

Xi has supported the return of ancient Chinese ideas, like [Confucianism](https://kids.kiddle.co/Confucianism "Confucianism"). He has said that the Western world is facing a "crisis of confidence." He believes the CCP is a "loyal inheritor and promoter of China's outstanding traditional culture."

Xi's leadership has also seen a rise in the ancient philosophy of [Legalism](https://kids.kiddle.co/Legalism_(Chinese_philosophy) "Legalism (Chinese philosophy)"). He has quoted thinkers like [Han Fei](https://kids.kiddle.co/Han_Fei "Han Fei"). He has also supported the philosopher [Wang Yangming](https://kids.kiddle.co/Wang_Yangming "Wang Yangming"). Xi has called for a "new marriage and childbirth culture."

He has emphasized using "red resources," which means remembering the history of the Communist Party. He believes art should serve political goals and national rejuvenation. He has also overseen a revival of traditional Chinese culture. He calls it the "soul" of the nation. He has established "four matters of confidence" for Chinese people. These are confidence in China's path, theories, political system, and culture.

### Ideology and Governance

Xi has stated that "only socialism can save China." He believes that socialism with Chinese characteristics is the right path for China's future. Some observers see Xi as a strong believer in communist ideas. He has emphasized that the Communist Party's goal is to achieve communism.

Xi believes that "capitalism is bound to die out and socialism bound to win." He has increased the study of "Socialist Political Economy With Chinese Characteristics" in China. He has also said that "the party leads them all," meaning the CCP leads all parts of government, military, and society.

He has stated that "without the Communist Party of China, there would be no new China." He believes the party's leadership is China's greatest strength. However, he also warns that the party must be careful to avoid collapse. Xi has spoken against "historical nihilism," which means challenging the party's official view of history.

Xi has rejected a [multi-party system](https://kids.kiddle.co/Multi-party_system "Multi-party system") for China. He believes China's "socialist democracy is the most comprehensive, genuine and effective democracy." This idea is different from Western democracies. He has also promoted "Chinese-style modernization," which he says is different from Western ways of modernizing.

#### Xi Jinping Thought

[![Image 16: A political slogan on the wall in Longhua District, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China, picture1](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/7/75/A_political_slogan_on_the_wall_in_Longhua_District%2C_Shenzhen%2C_Guangdong%2C_China%2C_picture1.jpg/300px-A_political_slogan_on_the_wall_in_Longhua_District%2C_Shenzhen%2C_Guangdong%2C_China%2C_picture1.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:A_political_slogan_on_the_wall_in_Longhua_District,_Shenzhen,_Guangdong,_China,_picture1.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:A_political_slogan_on_the_wall_in_Longhua_District,_Shenzhen,_Guangdong,_China,_picture1.jpg "Enlarge")

 A billboard promoting Xi Jinping Thought in [Shenzhen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Shenzhen "Shenzhen")

In September 2017, the CCP decided that Xi's political ideas would become part of the Party Constitution. These ideas are called "Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era." In March 2018, China's state constitution was also changed to include this thought.

[![Image 17: 201901 Xi Jinping's books at Shanghai Library](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/e/eb/201901_Xi_Jinping%27s_books_at_Shanghai_Library.jpg/300px-201901_Xi_Jinping%27s_books_at_Shanghai_Library.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:201901_Xi_Jinping%27s_books_at_Shanghai_Library.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:201901_Xi_Jinping%27s_books_at_Shanghai_Library.jpg "Enlarge")

_The Governance of China_ in different languages presented at Shanghai Library

Xi describes his thought as part of the larger framework of socialism with Chinese characteristics. This framework was started by [Deng Xiaoping](https://kids.kiddle.co/Deng_Xiaoping "Deng Xiaoping"). Official documents say Xi Jinping Thought continues the ideas of [Marxism–Leninism](https://kids.kiddle.co/Marxism "Marxism") and previous Chinese leaders. It is sometimes called "21st century Marxism." The ideas are explained in Xi's book series, _The Governance of China_. An app called _Xuexi Qiangguo_ was launched in 2019 to help people learn about Xi Jinping Thought.

## Personal Life

### Family Life

[![Image 18: Peng Liyuan, Xi Jinping and Barack Obama in the Lincoln Bedroom](https://kids.kiddle.co/images/thumb/0/0b/Peng_Liyuan%2C_Xi_Jinping_and_Barack_Obama_in_the_Lincoln_Bedroom.jpg/300px-Peng_Liyuan%2C_Xi_Jinping_and_Barack_Obama_in_the_Lincoln_Bedroom.jpg)](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Peng_Liyuan,_Xi_Jinping_and_Barack_Obama_in_the_Lincoln_Bedroom.jpg)

[](https://kids.kiddle.co/Image:Peng_Liyuan,_Xi_Jinping_and_Barack_Obama_in_the_Lincoln_Bedroom.jpg "Enlarge")

 Xi Jinping, [Peng Liyuan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Peng_Liyuan "Peng Liyuan") and U.S. president [Barack Obama](https://kids.kiddle.co/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") in the Lincoln Bedroom

Xi's first marriage was to Ke Lingling. They divorced after a few years. In 1987, Xi married [Peng Liyuan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Peng_Liyuan "Peng Liyuan"), a famous Chinese folk singer. Peng was more famous than Xi until he became a top political leader. She has taken on a more public role as China's "first lady" than previous leaders' wives. For example, she hosted U.S. First Lady [Michelle Obama](https://kids.kiddle.co/Michelle_Obama "Michelle Obama") in 2014.

Xi and Peng have a daughter named Xi Mingze. She graduated from [Harvard University](https://kids.kiddle.co/Harvard_University "Harvard University") in 2015. She used a different name while studying there.

### Personality and Interests

Peng Liyuan has described Xi as hardworking and down-to-earth. She said that at home, he is "just my husband." Journalists who met him in the past described him as confident and relaxed. He was seen as practical, serious, and hardworking. Chinese state media often shows him as a caring leader who stands up for China.

Xi is a big fan of soccer. He has a vision to make China a soccer superpower. He wants China to qualify for the World Cup, host a World Cup, and eventually win one. In 2015, he approved a plan to include soccer in school and build many soccer schools.

Unlike previous leaders, more is known about Xi's private life, though it is still carefully managed. He reportedly swims and walks every day. He enjoys foreign writers, especially Russian authors like [Leo Tolstoy](https://kids.kiddle.co/Leo_Tolstoy "Leo Tolstoy"). He also likes films and TV shows such as _[Saving Private Ryan](https://kids.kiddle.co/Saving\_Private\_Ryan "Saving Private Ryan")_ and _[The Godfather](https://kids.kiddle.co/The\_Godfather "The Godfather")_.

[Indonesia](https://kids.kiddle.co/Indonesia "Indonesia") first joined the [Olympic Games](https://kids.kiddle.co/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games") in 1952. Since then, Indonesian athletes have competed in almost every [Summer Olympic Games](https://kids.kiddle.co/Summer_Olympic_Games "Summer Olympic Games"). They missed only two Games: in 1964 and 1980. In 1964, they were banned because of a disagreement during the 1962 Asian Games. In 1980, they joined a boycott led by the U.S. The [National Olympic Committee](https://kids.kiddle.co/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") for Indonesia was formed in 1946 and officially recognized in 1952. Indonesia has never taken part in the [Winter Olympic Games](https://kids.kiddle.co/Winter_Olympic_Games "Winter Olympic Games"). This is because the country does not have many places for winter sports.

As of 2024, Indonesian athletes have won a total of 40 medals. Most of these medals, 22, are from [badminton](https://kids.kiddle.co/Badminton_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Badminton at the Summer Olympics"). They also won 16 medals in [weightlifting](https://kids.kiddle.co/Weightlifting_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Weightlifting at the Summer Olympics"), one in [archery](https://kids.kiddle.co/Archery_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Archery at the Summer Olympics"), and one in [sport climbing](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sport_climbing_at_the_Summer_Olympics "Sport climbing at the Summer Olympics"). Among countries in Southeast Asia, Indonesia is second in both gold medals (10) and total medals (40), right after [Thailand](https://kids.kiddle.co/Thailand_at_the_Olympics "Thailand at the Olympics").

Indonesia's first Olympic medal was a silver. It was won by archers Lilies Handayani, Nurfitriyana Saiman, and Kusuma Wardhani in the women's team event at the [1988 Seoul Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1988_Summer_Olympics "1988 Summer Olympics"). The country's first two gold medals came in 1992 at the [Barcelona Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics"). These were won by Susi Susanti and Alan Budikusuma in badminton singles. They later got married! The 1992 Games were also the first time Indonesia won more than one gold medal. Since then, Indonesia has won at least one gold medal at every Olympic Games, except for the [2012 London Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2012_Summer_Olympics "2012 Summer Olympics").

In badminton, Indonesia is one of only two countries, along with [China](https://kids.kiddle.co/China_at_the_Olympics "China at the Olympics"), to have won gold medals in all five types of badminton events at the Olympics.

Indonesia's newest gold medalist is Rizki Juniansyah. He won the men's 73 kg weightlifting event in 2024. He even broke an Olympic record! At 21 years old, he became the youngest Indonesian to win an Olympic gold medal. He beat the record set by Susi Susanti in 1992. His gold medal came just hours after his teammate Veddriq Leonardo won the speed event in sport climbing. Both men were the first Indonesians to win Olympic gold medals in sports other than badminton. With two gold medals, the [2024 Paris Olympics](https://kids.kiddle.co/2024_Summer_Olympics "2024 Summer Olympics") was Indonesia's best Olympic performance since 1992.

The **President of China** is the official leader who represents the [People's Republic of China](https://kids.kiddle.co/China "China"). This role is mostly ceremonial, meaning it has many duties like a [head of state](https://kids.kiddle.co/Head_of_state "Head of state") but doesn't hold much real power on its own. However, since 1993, the person who is President also holds other very powerful positions. This includes being the leader of the [Chinese Communist Party](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") (CCP) and the head of the military. This makes the President the _de facto_ (actual) top leader of China.

The President's job is part of China's unique government system, where the [National People's Congress](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_People%27s_Congress "National People's Congress") (NPC) is the highest power. The President works with the NPC's Standing Committee to do things a head of state would normally do in other countries. For example, the President can deal with international matters if the NPC Standing Committee agrees.

## History of the Presidency

### Early Beginnings

The idea of a state representative in China goes back to 1912. That's when [Sun Yat-sen](https://kids.kiddle.co/Sun_Yat-sen "Sun Yat-sen") became the first leader of the [Republic of China](https://kids.kiddle.co/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949) "Republic of China (1912–1949)"). The current form of the presidency started on October 1, 1949. It was first called the Chairman of the Central People's Government.

### The 1954 Constitution

In 1954, China created a new Constitution. This document officially set up the role of "state chairman." This chairman had some ceremonial powers, similar to today's President. The chairman also had military powers, leading the armed forces and the National Defence Council. They could also call special meetings with top government officials.

[Mao Zedong](https://kids.kiddle.co/Mao_Zedong "Mao Zedong"), a very important leader, was the first state chairman. He was elected in 1954.

### Changes and Abolition

In 1959, [Liu Shaoqi](https://kids.kiddle.co/Liu_Shaoqi "Liu Shaoqi") became the state chairman. He was re-elected in 1965. However, during the [Cultural Revolution](https://kids.kiddle.co/Cultural_Revolution "Cultural Revolution") in 1966, Liu Shaoqi lost his power. In 1968, he was officially removed from all his positions, including state chairman. This was against the Constitution, which said only the NPC could remove him. After Liu was removed, the position of state chairman was empty.

In 1975, China adopted a new Constitution that completely removed the state chairman position. The duties of representing the state were given to the chairman of the NPC Standing Committee instead. This change emphasized that the Communist Party was in charge of everything.

### The Presidency Returns in 1982

In 1982, the presidency was brought back with a new Constitution. Leaders decided it was important to have a President to represent the country. However, they wanted the President to have limited powers. The idea was for the President to be a symbolic figure, like a president in a country with a parliament. The real power was meant to be with the leader of the Communist Party, the Premier (head of government), and the head of the military.

At first, these top jobs were held by different people. But in 1993, [Jiang Zemin](https://kids.kiddle.co/Jiang_Zemin "Jiang Zemin") became President. He was already the leader of the Communist Party and the military. This made him the undisputed top leader of China. Since then, the President of China has also been the most powerful person in the Party and the military.

In 2018, a big change happened. The rule that limited the President to two terms was removed. This means the President can now serve for an unlimited number of terms. [Xi Jinping](https://kids.kiddle.co/Xi_Jinping "Xi Jinping"), the current President, explained this change was to match the presidency with his other powerful roles, which don't have term limits.

## How the President is Chosen

### Who Can Be President?

To become President, a person must:

*   Be a Chinese citizen.
*   Have the right to vote and be elected.
*   Be at least 45 years old.

### The Election Process

The President is chosen by the [National People's Congress](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_People%27s_Congress "National People's Congress") (NPC). The NPC's executive body, called the Presidium, suggests a candidate. In reality, the [Chinese Communist Party](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party") decides who will be nominated. So far, only one candidate has ever been nominated for the presidency.

The NPC then votes to elect the President. They can also vote to remove the President from office. Both decisions are made by a majority vote. The President serves for five years, which is the same length as the NPC's term. Since 2018, the President must take an oath to the Constitution before starting their job.

## What the President Does

The President represents China both inside the country and to other nations. The Constitution says the presidency is a state body that performs state activities.

The President has several powers, but most of them need the approval of the [National People's Congress](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_People%27s_Congress "National People's Congress") (NPC). These powers include:

*   Announcing new laws.
*   Choosing and removing the Premier (head of government) and other ministers.
*   Granting pardons (forgiveness for crimes).
*   Declaring states of emergency.
*   Issuing orders for large-scale actions.
*   Giving out state awards.
*   Appointing and removing ambassadors to other countries.
*   Signing and canceling treaties with foreign countries.

One special power is conducting state visits to other countries. This is the only power that doesn't need NPC oversight. Because most presidential powers need NPC approval, the President is mainly a symbolic figure. They don't have direct control over how the government runs.

The President also suggests who should be the Premier. While the NPC confirms this choice, they have never rejected a nomination. The Premier is a very important job, so this power can give the President some influence.

## Line of Succession

If the President's office becomes empty, the [Vice President](https://kids.kiddle.co/Vice_President_of_China "Vice President of China") takes over. If both offices become empty, the chairman of the NPC Standing Committee temporarily acts as President. This continues until the NPC can elect a new President and Vice President.

The **Premier of China** is a very important leader in [China](https://kids.kiddle.co/China "China"). This person is officially called the "Premier of the State Council of the People's Republic of China". They are the head of the [State Council](https://kids.kiddle.co/State_Council_of_the_People%27s_Republic_of_China "State Council of the People's Republic of China"), which is like China's main government cabinet. The Premier is also the [head of government](https://kids.kiddle.co/Head_of_government "Head of government") and holds the highest position in China's public service.

## Contents

*   [What Does the Premier Do?](https://kids.kiddle.co/Premier_of_China#What_Does_the_Premier_Do.3F)
*   [How is the Premier Chosen?](https://kids.kiddle.co/Premier_of_China#How_is_the_Premier_Chosen.3F)
    *   [Term Length and Party Role](https://kids.kiddle.co/Premier_of_China#Term_Length_and_Party_Role)

*   [Who is the Current Premier?](https://kids.kiddle.co/Premier_of_China#Who_is_the_Current_Premier.3F)
*   [See Also](https://kids.kiddle.co/Premier_of_China#See_Also)

## What Does the Premier Do?

The Premier leads the State Council, which is in charge of running the country's day-to-day affairs. Think of them as the chief executive who makes sure the government's plans are carried out. They oversee different government departments and make important decisions about the economy, education, and other public services.

## How is the Premier Chosen?

The Premier is officially approved by the [National People's Congress](https://kids.kiddle.co/National_People%27s_Congress "National People's Congress"). This is China's highest state power. The [President](https://kids.kiddle.co/President_of_China "President of China") suggests who should be the Premier. However, the person is usually chosen through a special process within the [Communist Party of China](https://kids.kiddle.co/Chinese_Communist_Party "Chinese Communist Party").

### Term Length and Party Role

Both the President and the Premier are chosen for a five-year term. They can serve for two terms. The Premier is always a member of the powerful [Politburo Standing Committee](https://kids.kiddle.co/CPC_Politburo_Standing_Committee "CPC Politburo Standing Committee"). This group is made up of the top leaders in the Communist Party.

## Who is the Current Premier?

The current Premier of China is [Li Keqiang](https://kids.kiddle.co/Li_Keqiang "Li Keqiang"). He started his role on March 15, 2013.

Title: Strivon on Instagram: "At the 2016 Rio Olympics, South African sprinter Wayde van Niekerk rewrote history in the men’s 400 metres. Starting from the outside lane 8 normally considered a disadvantage he exploded out of the blocks and ran the perfect race against the clock. With pure power and flawless pacing, he stopped the clock at a breathtaking 43.03 seconds, smashing Michael Johnson’s 17-year-old world record of 43.18 that had stood since 1999. 

This wasn’t just a new mark it was a statement that redefined one-lap sprinting. Van Niekerk became the first man ever to win Olympic 400 m gold from lane 8 and delivered one of the greatest one-lap performances in track and field history. His run remains the fastest 400 m ever, a feat of speed, strategy and sheer will that still challenges every generation of sprinters.

[![Image 15: Athletics South Africa (ASA) Cross Country Championship 2023 in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape Province, 16 September 2023. The Athletics South Africa, Eastern Province Athletics and the Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality hosted the Cross Country championships on 16 September 2023 at the Nelson Mandela University Sports Fields in Gqeberha, Eastern Cape. Athletics South Africa the controlling authority ensured that the event ran smoothly as Cross Country is one of the toughest disciplines in running. The regions under Athletics South Africa with most of the regions attending the Cross Country competition as far as Western Province to Mpumalanga. The South African National Defence Force participated with 18 members from the South African Army. Two members from the South African Air Force under the management of Lieutenant Colonel M.G. Soke, Staff Sergeant K. Aphane and Lance Corporal J.S. Tshikovhi. One of the SA National Defence's top achievements was Staff Sergeant Samson Mkhize obtaining 3rd position in the age category of males 50-55. # Badminton World Federation (BWF)

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) is recognised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) as the world governing body for badminton. The International Badminton Federation (IBF), as it was originally called, was established in London, on 5 July 1934 with nine founding member associations. The BWF is a federation of 196 members.

The ITA is supporting BWF with the delivery of their anti-doping program since September 2020.

Markdown Content:
# World Badminton Museum

_A collection of materials highlighting the history of Badminton, focused on items that are not available elsewhere but also including collections of existing items curated for user convenience. If you have any materials to help complete the various collections or start a new one please consider submitting them._

*   Badminton in Media
    *   [Fine Art](link_0)_Badminton has been portrayed in many pieces of artwork over the ages._
    *   [Comics](link_1) - _art and humor combined_
    *   [Movies](link_2) - _movies and shows that contain Badminton references_

*   [Laws](link_3)_Laws of Badminton going back to the first organized play (1873-present)_
*   [Patents](link_4)_There have been many inventions related to shuttles and rackets that have revolutionized our sport._
*   [Research](link_5)_Serious research has been done by various groups over the years. A common and very difficult topic is flight characteristics of shuttlecocks. A sampling of research is included here- much more can be found elsewhere._
*   [Postage Stamps](link_6)
*   [Currency](link_7)
*   **International Badminton**  
_BAE provided the de-facto governance of Badminton until the founding of the IBF (International Badminton Federation) which was sited in England. In 2006 the organization was renamed BWF (Badminton World Federation) and moved to Malaysia. There have been various publications both by the official organizations and other private groups._
    *   IBF
        *   Handbook _(1936-2005) - annual publication detailing the year's events and results_
        *   [World Badminton](link_8)_(1972-1999)_

    *   BWF
        *   Handbook _(2006-present) - annual publication detailing the year's events and results_
        *   [Heritage Working Group](link_9)_- an effort to organize the collection and preservation of Badminton culture and history. [10FEB2024]_
        *   [Shuttle World](link_10) - _(2013-present) - official publication of the BWF [23JUN2022]_
        *   BWF Badminton Museum - _opening 2026 in Qingdao, China. Modern highlights of the history and status of Badminton. [Overview from AGM 2026](link_11)._ _[13MAY2026]_

    *   [Danish Badminton Museum](link_12) - _includes complete set of publications ([Badminton](link_13) and [Badminton Revue](link_14)) going back to 1949.[18OCT2021]_
    *   [Badminton Museum of Ireland](link_15)_- includes an outstanding collection of historical photos_ _[18OCT2021]_
    *   [Badminton Museum of Thailand](link_16)_[18OCT2021]_
    *   Publications
        *   [Miscellany](link_17)
        *   [Shuttlenws](link_18)_frequent reports from the mid to late 1990's published by an independent group of Badminton enthusiasts_

    *   Tournaments
        *   [Thomas Cup](link_19)_Men's team world championships_
        *   [Uber Cup](link_20)_Women's team world championships_
        *   [Sudirman Cup](link_21)_Mixed team world championships_
        *   [Olympics](link_22)

    *   People

*   **England Badminton**
    *   Milton Keynes _- for the definitive badminton museum see England's [National Badminton Museum](link_23) which houses artifacts dating back to the very first organized play in the late 1800's.[20MAY2025]_
    *   Publications
        *   [The Badminton Gazette](link_24)_(1907-1979)_
        *   [Badminton](link_25)_(1979-1982)_
        *   [Badminton Now](link_26)_(1982-1991)_
        *   [Badminton](link_25)_(1991-2009)_
        *   [Courtside Magazine](link_27)_(2009-??)_

    *   Tournaments
        *   [All England](link_28)

*   **[United States Badminton](link_29)**  
_There have been three governing bodies for Badminton in the United States. ABA (American Badminton Association) existed until 1977 and was then reformed as USBA (United States Badminton Association). USBA remained until 1997 when it became [USAB](link_30) (USA Badminton)._
    *   Tournaments
        *   [US Senior International](link_31)s

    *   Badminton Publications
        *   [Badminton USA](link_32)

    *   Regions

  
_**[More...](link_29)**_
  
*   **Canada Badminton**  
_The official governing organization for the sport of badminton in Canada is [Badminton Canada](link_33)._
    *   Tournaments 
        *   [Canadian Masters](link_34)

    *   Badminton Publications 

    *   Regions

  
_**More...**_
  
*   **Americas Badminton**
    *   [Mexico Open](link_35)

  
*   **European Badminton**
    *   [Badminton Europe](link_36)_an online magazine covering Badminton in Europe since 2009[10JUN2022]_

  
*   **Asian Badminton**
    *   [Badminton Extreme](link_37)_Badminton Extreme Philippines was started in 2009 by badminton enthusiasts Kennevic and Kennie Asuncion. [17NOV2022]_

The
